title: Lansdowne Bridge & Sukkur Barrage
urduTitle: لینز ڈاؤن برج اور سکھر بیراج
description: Constructed in 1889, Lansdowne Bridge is a masterpiece of Victorian cantilever iron engineering crossing the Indus River. Coupled with the 66-span Sukkur Barrage, it forms one of Pakistan's most awe-inspiring riverfront vistas.
highlights: Sunset boat rides across the Indus River
Fresh fried Palla fish food stalls at riverfront
Spectacular illuminated night views from Lab-e-Mehran park

title: Sadhu Bela Island Temple
description: Founded in 1823 by Baba Bankhandi Maharaj, Sadhu Bela is an ornate marble temple complex situated on an island in the middle of the flowing Indus River, accessible only by wooden motorboats.
highlights: Exquisite carved white marble architecture and frescos
Serene island atmosphere isolated from city traffic
Ancient banyan trees and historic monastic courtyards

title: Kot Diji Fort
distanceFromCorridor: 28 km South of Sukkur (35 min drive)
description: Perched dramatically on a 110-foot-high limestone hill, Kot Diji (Fort Ahmadabad) was built in 1795 by Mir Sohrab Khan Talpur. Its massive 30-foot bastions overlook vast date palm orchards.
highlights: Colossal high-altitude fortifications and gun batteries
Adjacent pre-Harappan Kot Diji archaeological mound (3300 BCE)
Panoramic 360-degree views of Khairpur date palm groves

title: Satiyan Jo Astan (Seven Sisters)
description: Perched on a rocky yellow limestone bluff overlooking the Indus, this 17th-century complex is famous for its intricate glazed tiles, Sufi mausoleums, and legend of seven pious sisters.
highlights: Spectacular vantage point of riverboats and sunset reflections
Rich folklore and tranquil spiritual ambience

title: Mohenjo-Daro UNESCO World Heritage
urduTitle: موئن جو دڑو، وادی سندھ کی تہذیب
description: Built around 2500 BCE, Mohenjo-Daro ('Mound of the Dead') was one of the world's earliest major urban settlements. It features advanced drainage systems, grid-planned brick streets, and the famous Great Bath.
highlights: The Great Bath and Buddhist Stupa pinnacle
On-site Archaeological Museum with Priest-King replica & seals
Unmatched historical significance dating back 4,500+ years

title: Gorakh Hill Station
description: Known as the 'Murree of Sindh', Gorakh Hill sits at 5,688 feet (1,734 m) in the Kirthar Mountains. It offers sub-zero winter temperatures, pristine stargazing skies, and sweeping sunset views.
highlights: Breathtaking 4x4 off-road jeep ascent through rugged gorges
Campfires under the crystal-clear Milky Way galaxy
Chilly mountain breeze and panoramic sunrise points
